summary.en: If you think you are lost, STOP: Stop, Think, Observe, Plan. Usually the safest plan is to stay where you are, signal for help, and save your energy, water and phone battery.
summary.fil: Kapag sa tingin mo ay naligaw ka, STOP: Stop (Huminto), Think (Mag-isip), Observe (Magmasid), Plan (Magplano). Kadalasan, pinakaligtas ang manatili sa kinaroroonan, humingi ng tulong gamit ang signal, at tipirin ang lakas, tubig at baterya ng phone.

callForHelp.en: If you have signal, call 911 or the Philippine Red Cross hotline 143. Say which Trail you are on, the last Waypoint or landmark you passed, and what you can see around you. If there is no signal, stay put and signal: tap SOS at the top of the screen, then press and hold to fire the Flare, and blow a whistle three times.
callForHelp.fil: Kung may signal ka, tumawag sa 911 o sa hotline ng Philippine Red Cross na 143. Sabihin kung saang Trail ka, ang huling Waypoint o palatandaang nadaanan mo, at ano ang nakikita mo sa paligid. Kung walang signal, manatili sa kinaroroonan at magbigay ng signal: pindutin ang SOS sa itaas ng screen, saka pindutin nang matagal para paganahin ang Flare, at pumito nang tatlong beses.

en: Stop as soon as you think you are lost. Sit down, breathe and stay calm. Walking around in a panic usually makes it worse.
Think: How did you get here? Where did you last see the trail or a trail marker? How much daylight is left?
Observe: look and listen for landmarks, trail markers, voices or other sounds. Check the map and your position in Tahak; GPS works without signal.
Plan: unless you are completely sure of the way back to the trail, stay where you are. People who stay put are easier for searchers to find.

Signal: blow a whistle three short times, then repeat. Tap SOS at the top of the screen, then press and hold to fire the Flare (flashlight, screen and whistle). Use bright clothing or a mirror to be seen.
If you have to move, stay in open areas where you can be seen, and avoid thick brush and steep ground.
Ration your food and water, but keep drinking. Rest and do not overexert yourself. Save phone battery for calls and the Flare.
Before dark, get ready for the night: put on extra layers and rain gear, use an emergency blanket, and shelter from wind and rain.
Stay positive. Call out now and then so searchers can hear you.
fil: Huminto agad kapag sa tingin mo ay naligaw ka. Umupo, huminga at manatiling kalmado. Kadalasang lumalala ang sitwasyon kapag nagpapanic at palakad-lakad.
Mag-isip: Paano ka napunta rito? Saan mo huling nakita ang trail o ang marker nito? Ilang oras pa bago dumilim?
Magmasid: tumingin at makinig para sa mga palatandaan, trail marker, boses o iba pang tunog. Tingnan ang mapa at ang posisyon mo sa Tahak; gumagana ang GPS kahit walang signal.
Magplano: maliban kung siguradong-sigurado ka sa daan pabalik sa trail, manatili ka sa kinaroroonan mo. Mas madaling mahanap ng mga rescuer ang mga taong hindi umaalis sa puwesto.

Magbigay ng signal: pumito nang tatlong maiikling beses, saka ulitin. Pindutin ang SOS sa itaas ng screen, saka pindutin nang matagal para paganahin ang Flare (flashlight, screen at pito). Gumamit ng matingkad na damit o salamin para makita ka.
Kung kailangan mong gumalaw, manatili sa mga bukas na lugar kung saan ka makikita, at iwasan ang masukal na halaman at matarik na lupa.
Tipirin ang pagkain at tubig mo, pero patuloy na uminom. Magpahinga at huwag magpakapagod. Tipirin ang baterya ng phone para sa tawag at sa Flare.
Bago dumilim, maghanda para sa gabi: magsuot ng dagdag na damit at kapote, gumamit ng emergency blanket, at sumilong mula sa hangin at ulan.
Manatiling positibo. Sumigaw paminsan-minsan para marinig ka ng mga naghahanap.

en: Do not keep walking in the hope of finding the trail.
Do not panic or run.
Do not wait until dark to prepare for the night.
Do not use up your phone battery on things other than calls, your position and the Flare.
fil: Huwag ituloy ang paglalakad sa pag-asang makikita mo ang trail.
Huwag hintaying dumilim bago maghanda para sa gabi.
Huwag ubusin ang baterya ng phone sa ibang bagay maliban sa tawag, sa pagtingin ng posisyon mo at sa Flare.

en: Night is coming and you have no shelter or warm clothes. Hypothermia can happen even in mild weather.
Someone in the group is injured, very cold, confused or exhausted. Open the matching Guide.
Your water is running out.
Thunder, heavy rain or rising streams. Open the Lightning or Flash floods Guide.
fil: Padilim na at wala kang silungan o mainit na damit. Puwedeng magka-hypothermia kahit hindi gaanong malamig ang panahon.
May kasamang napinsala, giniginaw nang husto, nalilito o sobrang pagod. Buksan ang katugmang Guide.
Kulog, malakas na ulan o tumataas na ilog. Buksan ang Guide sa Kidlat o sa Biglaang baha.

review.notes: PRC basis: hotline only. No Philippine Red Cross material on being lost while hiking could be found; this is a wilderness-navigation topic, not first aid. The PRC source is cited only for hotline 143. STOP wording ('Stop, Think, Observe and Plan') from the NPS Glacier release. NYSDEC uses 'S is for Sit down' and gives the Think/Observe/Plan questions used in steps 2-4. WVDNR gives: stop moving and stay put, three short whistle blasts as the universal distress signal, whistle/mirror/bright clothing/flashlight, stay in open areas if you must move, conserve energy and stay hydrated, stay warm (hypothermia even in mild weather), stay positive and vocal. IFRC 'Remote context' supports learning how to signal for help. Tahak-specific lines (Flare via the SOS control, GPS position in Tahak works offline) describe app features, not first aid. CONTEXT.md says to avoid the term 'SOS button', so the Flare is described as 'tap SOS at the top of the screen, then press and hold' (matching the Flare screen's 'Hold to fire the Flare'), matching the shell's SOS control label. DISAGREEMENT: WVDNR also advises 'follow waterways' to find civilisation. This was deliberately left out because Philippine mountain streams often run into gorges and waterfalls and flood quickly; the reviewer may want a PH source (for example DENR or a mountaineering federation) on this. 'Ration food and water but keep drinking' combines NPS ('rationed their food') with WVDNR ('stay hydrated').
